subject: Proposal: Dedicated capacity amendment — GPUs for larger model + reranker
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Proposal: Dedicated capacity amendment — GPUs for larger model + reranker

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. As discussed, Beacon Health is planning to renew its Dedicated contract and add the new clinical-rank model and longer-context conversational model for triage workflows. Those two changes materially change the GPU profile (larger model + slower per-token throughput) and we should capture the capacity increase in an amendment to avoid throttles during peak hours.

High-level proposal attached: redwood_proposal_beacon_v2.pdf (summary + cost breakdown). Key points you asked to see: the needed additional reserved capacity (6x A100-equivalent GPUs in a dedicated pool), a throughput SLO for peak business hours (99th percentile latency target tied to the add-on), and a recommended reranker instance for post-processing (separate pool for isolating batch reranking).

Next steps I suggest:
- You review the attached proposal with procurement and legal.
- We update the term to include the extra capacity as a one-year committed pool with an option to scale at quarter renewals.
- If procurement needs a commercial summary only, I can send a two-page amendment and a single-sheet cost table.

Dev, can you confirm the latency/throughput numbers and whether we should propose a managed autoscale buffer for the reranker pool?

Sara — happy to hop on a follow-up with your procurement team Friday if that helps.

Thanks,
Priyom
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Proposal: Dedicated capacity amendment — GPUs for larger model + reranker

Priyom —

Thanks for the quick recap and proposal. I shared the docs with procurement and our ML infra lead. A few clarifying questions from our side:

1) Can you break out the cost impact of the larger LLM (1.2T param) versus the reranker separately? We need separate line-items for budget approval.
2) For the throughput SLO, we need a guarantee for peak-hour tail latency during our business hours (M–F, 7a–7p ET). Ideally something that lets us avoid manual throttling or falling back to a smaller model automatically.
3) Are there options to spread the commitment across regions? We run a small EU test deployment that may need best-effort capacity in Jan.

Procurement asked if Redwood can offer a 6–10% renewal credit for a one-year commit if we add the reranker as an add-on and sign this week. Is that negotiable?

Happy to do a quick call Friday at 10am ET to walk procurement through the numbers.

Best,
Sara Liu
Director, Product — Care Ops
Beacon Health

Hi all — thanks for the details. I pulled together numbers and a recommended amendment summary (attached in-line here).

Summary (short):
- 1.2T clinical model: recommended dedicated pool = 6x A100-equivalent GPUs (spotting for model size and context ~ 128k tokens/session). Expected average cost uplift: +64% compute vs current mix; see beacon_cost-breakdown_q4.xlsx for per-hour and monthly run-rates.
- Reranker: separate reserved pool of 2x A100-equivalent GPUs with managed autoscale buffer (+15% headroom). Rationale: batch reranking can be isolated to avoid noisy-neighbor impact and keep inference latency predictable.
- Throughput SLO: 99th percentile inference latency <= 450ms for single-request generation (up to 1k tokens) during business hours M–F 7a–7p ET. Fallback policy: automatic downgrade to 512-context variant of the model if sustained tail breaches >5 minutes; Redwood will notify via webhook and open incident.
- EU best-effort: we can allocate warm standby capacity in our eu-west-1 region (no hard SLA) for Jan test; if Beacon needs strict latency, we should formalize as multi-region add-on.
- Commercial: for a one-year commit covering the new capacity, we can offer a 7% renewal credit applied to monthly committed fees. Anything above 8% requires director approval.

Attachments: redwood_proposal_beacon_v2.pdf (updated), beacon_cost-breakdown_q4.xlsx (detailed rates)

Action items:
- Priyom: produce the one-page commercial amendment highlighting the 7% credit and SLO language.
- Neha: confirm approval for the 7% concession or route for director sign-off.
- Sara / Beacon Procurement: confirm whether procurement accepts a 7% credit and agrees to the fallback policy.

Sara — I can join Friday's 10am ET call and walk through the cost table and the SLO.

Regards,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
